summary: A light-to-medium abstract tile-drafting game where players take colored tiles from shared factory displays to build patterns on their own board, scoring for adjacency and completed rows while being careful not to get stuck with leftover penalty tiles. It's quick to teach, tense in a quiet way, and looks beautiful on the table.
praised: simple rules with surprisingly sharp tactical depth
criticised: can feel a bit solitaire-ish since boards develop independently

interaction.detail: Players draft tiles from shared factory displays and a shared center pool, and taking a color can leave undesirable leftovers for the next player or force them into penalty tiles. Each player then places tiles on their own private pattern board and wall, so the only shared game state is the tile supply, not the boards themselves.

sources: wall placement points each round (with adjacency bonuses)
floor line penalty for overflow tiles
end-game bonus for completed horizontal rows
end-game bonus for completed vertical columns
end-game bonus for completing a full color set
scoring.how_you_win: Draft tiles each round to fill pattern lines and transfer completed lines onto your wall for points, minus penalties for overflow; once someone completes a horizontal wall row the game ends after that round plus bonuses, and the highest total wins.
